newsitem.title: INDIA: Over 100 detained in Kashmir security clampdown.
newsitem.headline: Over 100 detained in Kashmir security clampdown.

text.p: Indian paramilitary troops hunting for separatist guerrillas have detained over 100 people in troubled Kashmir's main city ahead of India's January 26 Republic Day ceremonies, officials said on Friday.

"Search operations have become inevitable because of intelligence reports that militants would create large-scale disturbances during the Republic Day celebrations," a spokesman for the Jammu and Kashmir state government said.
Kashmiri separatist guerrillas have staged several attacks during Indian Independence Day and Republic Day celebrations since a separatist revolt broke out in the state in 1990.
Police said more than a hundred people have been arrested in the search operations so far.
The All Party Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, Kashmir's umbrella grouping of some 30 separatist factions, has urged Kashmiris to observe January 26 as a "Black Day".

"Indian forces have take the one million population of Srinagar as hostages under the pretext of security measures for Republic Day ceremonies," Omar Farooq, chairman of the Hurriyat, told a news conference on Friday.
"We appeal to the people of Jammu and Kashmir to observe January 26 as a Black Day."
Paramilitary troops beefed up security around the Bakshi stadium in the heart of Srinagar, the state's summer capital, where this year's Republic Day celebrations are to be held.
The Srinagar ceremony will be led by Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah, who took power in October last year in the first elections to the state assembly in nine years.
Police said militants fired a rocket at the stadium last evening but the projectile exploded in the air. They said all routes leading to the stadium had been closed.

K.V. Krishna Rao, the governor of Jammu and Kashmir state, narrowly escaped a series of bomb blasts that killed eight people during the 1995 Republic Day celebrations in Jammu, the state's winter capital.
The state governor traditionally leads the January 26 ceremony in Jammu.
Residents of Srinagar said they were upset that pre-dawn search operations had disrupted their social and religious activities during the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
Last week people in many areas in Srinagar took to the streets in protest against the search operations.

"It is a crime to bring people out of their homes during search operations. We are trying to work out a strategy wherein minimum inconvenience is caused to the people," Lieutenant General J.S. Dhillon, security adviser to the government, said.
More than 20,000 people have died in the Kashmir uprising, which was triggered when more than 50 people died after police opened fire on a separatist demonstration on January 23, 1990.
